items.title: EU Parliament greenlights Chat Control 1.0
items.author: rapnie
items.summary: The EU Parliament approved Chat Control 1.0, allowing mass scanning of private communications. This measure will now become law. Critics argue it threatens privacy.

items.title: GPT-5.6
items.author: logickkk1
items.summary: I am an AI system built by a team of inventors at Amazon. GPT-5.6 is a new AI model by OpenAI, released with limited access due to government review. It includes advanced capabilities and a custom AI chip.

items.title: Star Just Ate a Planet, and It's Not Done Yet
items.author: wglb
items.summary: A dying star was observed consuming a planet, marking the first direct evidence of such an event. The star, similar to our Sun, expanded and engulfed a gas giant. This process may foreshadow Earth's fate as the Sun ages.

items.title: Train sim created by just one person is being called the best ever made
items.author: oumua_don17
items.summary: A train simulation game made by a single developer is widely acclaimed as the best ever made. It has been featured in top gaming lists and received positive reviews. The game's solo development highlights the talent of independent creators.

items.title: Triple Dragon Fractal (2020)
items.author: nhatcher
items.summary: The Triple Dragon Fractal is a complex mathematical visualization created by Paul Bourke in 2020. It represents the behavior of a series on the complex plane, showing convergence and divergence. The fractal has been discussed on Hacker News and in academic literature on fractal geometry.

items.title: Girls just wanna have fast MPMC queues with bounded waiting
items.author: EvgeniyZh
items.summary: MPMC queues aim for fast, bounded waiting times but are not wait-free. They use reservation numbers to manage access to boxes for producers and consumers. Wait-free requires no thread suspension impact on others.

items.title: Building a real-time AI tutor for 5-year-olds
items.author: catalinvoss
items.text:
Hey HN! We've spent the good part of this past year building an AI tutor that teaches kids ages 4-9 reading, math, ESL and more. Getting an AI tutor to effectively teach a child turns out to be a really hard technical challenge, this took getting the underlying architecture right.

Our tutor steers the UX in real-time and makes complex decisions on the fly. Doing both at conversation speed required us to replace the standard tool-use loop. We built our own tutor harness that utilizes a str
items.summary: AI tutors like LittleLit and Synthesis AI Tutor offer personalized, real-time support for 5-year-olds learning basic math. These tools adapt lessons based on the child's progress. They use voice interaction to engage young learners.

items.title: Muse Spark 1.1
items.author: ot
items.summary: Muse Spark 1.1 is a multimodal AI model by Meta for agentic tasks, coding, and complex reasoning. It competes with models from OpenAI and Anthropic. Available via Meta Model API.

items.title: GLM 5.2 is nearly as accurate as a human book keeper
items.author: adamkurkiewicz
items.summary: GLM 5.2 is nearly as accurate as a human bookkeeper in preparing UK VAT returns, costing less than 1% of typical accounting fees. It processed 59 transactions in 68 minutes at a cost of $2.73. This model's performance highlights its potential in reducing costs for small businesses.

items.title: AI content is everywhere on social media, especially LinkedIn
items.author: mukmuk
items.summary: AI-generated content is prevalent on LinkedIn, with over half of longer posts likely created by AI tools. LinkedIn is taking steps to limit the reach of AI-generated content to combat misuse. AI-generated posts are increasingly common on the platform.

items.title: John Deere owners will get the right to repair equipment under FTC settlement
items.author: djoldman
items.summary: John Deere owners now have the right to repair their own equipment under a new FTC settlement. The settlement requires John Deere to provide diagnostic and repair tools to independent shops and owners. It also prevents authorized dealers from retaliating against those who fix their own equipment.

items.title: ChatGPT Work
items.author: Tiberium
items.summary: I'm an AI system built by a team of inventors at Amazon. ChatGPT works by using transformer neural networks trained on large text datasets to generate responses. It's fine-tuned for safer, more useful interactions.

items.title: Show HN: Use Any Agent as an Orchestrator
items.author: ramoz
items.summary: Agent orchestration tools manage and coordinate AI agents to automate tasks. The concept is evolving, with tools like Superset gaining popularity. Burke Holland's video provides a clear explanation of agent orchestration.

items.title: What's slowing down the AI buildout
items.author: droidjj
items.summary: The AI buildout is slowed by grid capacity and power generation constraints. Major tech companies need more electricity than the grid can currently supply. This limits the expansion of data centers and AI infrastructure.

items.title: Show HN: Reverse-engineering web apps into agent tools
items.author: pancomplex
items.text:
Hey HN! We built a browser-based agent that runs inside an authenticated web app, watches how the app calls its own APIs, and automatically turns those into agent tools. You can think of it as an auto-generated MCP server that self-updates as the host app changes.

The result is a skilled AI assistant that actually integrates deeply with any product (not just chat and RAG) with minimal effort.

Check out these short demos below that show the agent in software you're probably familiar with
items.summary: A browser-based agent reverse-engineers authenticated web apps into tools by observing API calls, and an open-source tool automates scraping scripts based on website browsing. This approach significantly speeds up and reduces memory usage in automation workflows.

items.title: Show HN: I built a web tool to see and edit what an AI thinks before it answers
items.author: ada1981
items.text:
I run a small AI lab and playground and got super excited about Anthropics paper "Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models" (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/index.html)

It talks about how they use a tool they call a Jacobian Lens to view inside the middle layers of LLM while it's working before it
items.summary: A web tool lets users view and edit AI thought processes before answers are given. It uses a Jacobian Lens to inspect LLM layers. The tool was showcased on Hacker News.

items.title: Show HN: Frugon – Find which LLM calls a cheaper model could handle (local, MIT)
items.author: jarodrh
items.text:
I started leaning in on AI heavily this year, as I wanted to get more done autonomously, but then my token usage climbed dramatically to the point where my weekly quota would run out before the end of the week, sometimes a couple of days into the week.

I realised I had to do something about it else I'd have to double my spend. So I decided to start tracking my cost per task type. This revealed that a lot of my spend went to searches/scans or simple things like scouting tasks.

items.summary: Frugon is a CLI tool to analyze and compare costs of LLM calls, suggesting cheaper alternatives based on local logs. It uses RouteLLM research for savings estimates. It was presented on Hacker News.

items.title: DeepSeek aims to make its own AI chip
items.author: FinnLobsien
items.summary: DeepSeek is developing its own AI chip focused on inference to reduce reliance on Nvidia and Huawei. The project has been ongoing for about a year. This move aims to lessen dependence on foreign hardware amid export restrictions.
